subject: Surinam toad
title: This Toad Hunts in the Dark With 128 Supersensitive Fingertips

scenes.text: This frog catches fish in pitch-black water. Its eyes are tiny.
The Surinam toad waits in murky Amazon water, arms spread wide.
Each finger ends in a star of sixteen soft tips. One hundred twenty-eight in all.
They're eight percent of its arm's skin, but packed with touch nerves, as sensitive as your fingertips.
When a fish swims close, the tips feel the water move, and the toad snaps it up.
It doesn't need to see. It reads the water with its hands.

description:
The Surinam toad hunts fish in murky Amazon water using star-shaped fingertips.
A 2026 UCLA study found 16 soft tips on each of its eight fingers, covering about 8% of the forelimb's skin but packed with touch nerves, with a huge share of its brain devoted to them.
Which would you rather have: better eyes or fingertips like these?
first_comment: Young Surinam toads start with just four tips per finger. Would you trade your eyesight for fingertips that can feel a fish swim by?
